title: Laser
coreMove: Prepare the environment so the next distraction has to cross a barrier before it can break the Highlight.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar identifies Laser as the practical work of fighting distraction from devices, apps, and other pulls so a focus block can hold.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong generic version says focus harder or turn off notifications. The specific move is to build friction before attention is under attack, so flow has a protected route.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital radiology scheduler protecting a tumor-board prep block
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator whose devices create constant openings for interruption
exampleSpecs.stakes: the oncology team starts with missing scans if prep is fragmented
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she forwards nonurgent calls to the backup line, places the scan list on the left monitor, and removes the messaging app from view before starting the focus block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tumor-board scan list glowing beside a muted call console

exampleSpecs.domain: a conservation cartographer tracing illegal logging boundaries
exampleSpecs.audience: a map specialist who loses flow to satellite-feed alerts and chat requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: the enforcement report fails if the boundary line is sloppy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he exports the needed imagery first, disconnects the live alert feed, and starts Laser only after the mapping tools are open and the chat route is blocked
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a jagged logging scar visible across a satellite tile

exampleSpecs.domain: a theater lighting designer programming cues before tech rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a creative technician whose focus gets broken by app pings and hallway requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: actors hit a blackout if the cue stack remains half programmed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, she programs while answering every production ping; after, she posts the cue-range target on the console and hands the stage manager a written interruption rule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: blue wash light spilling over a lighting console with cue 47 selected

exampleSpecs.domain: a forensic accountant reviewing a charity fraud ledger
exampleSpecs.audience: an investigator needing sustained pattern recognition rather than scattered checking
exampleSpecs.stakes: a hidden transfer chain is missed if focus resets every few minutes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after missing the transfer pattern, she rebuilds the next session by printing the ledger slice, locking the case chat until noon, and keeping only the bank-reference file open
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a highlighted transfer column running down a printed ledger page

exampleSpecs.domain: a marine mechanic diagnosing an intermittent ferry engine fault
exampleSpecs.audience: a tradesperson whose attention gets broken by dockside questions
exampleSpecs.stakes: the fault returns during the afternoon crossing if the diagnostic sequence is interrupted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he tells the deckhand the next forty minutes are Laser time, clips a laminated do-not-route card to the engine-room rail, and follows the diagnostic sequence without answering dock questions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grease-marked diagnostic sheet clipped under a vibrating engine-room gauge

exampleSpecs.domain: a grant illustrator finishing anatomical plates for a medical textbook
exampleSpecs.audience: a visual specialist who needs flow for precision work
exampleSpecs.stakes: a mislabeled nerve path survives proofing if attention keeps snapping away
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she notes the exact app that broke flow yesterday, removes the tablet's social dock before drawing, and begins with the nerve plate already open at full screen
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a half-rendered brachial plexus plate enlarged on a drawing tablet

skillTargets: identify which distraction route must be blocked before a focus block starts
choose friction that fits the task rather than a symbolic digital cleanse
analyze why a focus attempt failed by locating the unblocked route
evaluate whether a proposed Laser tactic protects the Highlight or merely signals seriousness

tryThisNowSpec: Before the next focus block, name the one distraction route most likely to break it and add one barrier that requires a physical or procedural step to cross.

rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm -- a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
